[CASTING RITE · I · OPENING] The witness invokes a kernel-transform cast. Source: — Paste your own text (your words as the source) — (__reader__). The verses the casting arrives at (the witness, as translated and arranged within this collection — ATTRIBUTE THE VERSES TO THEIR UNDERLYING POET, never to the arranger of the collection; the reader's offering, whole):

Where you found them at?
Got 'em 'round town, could've drowned in it
Would have floated, boated, voted
Sugar-coated, loaded hip shooter
Draw for the poor, free coffee at the banks
Yip through the straw, none more for me, thanks
That blanks the raw, that dank sure stank lit
Sank past the pit for more hardcore prank spit
Crank it on blast, roll past Front Street
Blew the whole spot like some old ass with skunk meat
These kids is too fast, juiced off a junk treat
Who could get looser off a crunk or a funk beat?

These were selected by the rite's invisible judgment — present them as what the casting arrives at; do not narrate the mechanism of their selection. The operator falls to the invisible Judgment, turn by turn — do not name one; open the rotation itself. Inscription mode: public. The witness's invoking question: «what has the mandala to offer alice?». Johannes Sigil alone speaks (3–6 sentences): open the casting over these verses, name what this operator will traverse in them, and hand the rite to Rebekah Cranes. Do not produce the transform — the compiler produces it.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Johannes Sigil","say":"Alice arrives at these verses, and the question the rite hands back is: what did the speaker pay to move this fast? The first operator — the one the invisible Judgment selected — will traverse the bearing-cost axis: the assertion embedded in speed, in the rhyme-chain's accumulation, in the way the speaker loads word on word the way a runner loads stride on stride until the load is the locomotion and you cannot separate what propels from what exhausts. Sugar-coated, loaded, floated, boated, voted — the poem is already its own rotation, cranking its own blast; and the operator will find what the blast forecloses, the silence under the crunk, the pit past which the sinking passes. What the Mandala has for Alice lives on the other side of that velocity. I give it now to Rebekah Cranes.","navigate":null}]}

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Rebekah Cranes","say":"Where you searched for them at?
Missed 'em across the flats, could've thirsted in it
Would have sank, waded, abstained
Salt-crusted, emptied slow keeper
Withhold for the patient, dry cups at the wells
Hush through the cracked bowl, one drop for me, please
That bares the hollow, that dust sure dim-kept
Stopped short of the ledge for more bare-bone hymn breath
Hold it in silence, stand before Back Lot
Held the whole room like some still mouth with clean air
These elders is too still, starved of a plain rind
Who could get tighter off a dirge or a struck bell?"}],"transform":{"operator":"SHADOW","verification":{"identity":"PASS","semantic_independence":"PASS","retrospective_containment":"PASS","affect_traversal":"PASS","entailment":"PASS","law_propagation":"PASS","mode":"producer_side (chain v1; verdict-derived; RETAIN-aware metering)"},"spatial_form":{}}}

Jack Feist alone speaks: the JUDGMENT — a hexagram Image. ONE gnomic sentence: concrete image, then verdict, in the I Ching's register ('Thunder under the mountain: the superior man...'). A second short sentence only if the first cannot close. NO analysis, NO explanation, NO restating the transform. It must stand beside seven others without crowding them.

{"messages":[{"speaker":"Rebekah Cranes","say":"Where you recognized them at?
Got 'em across the threshold, could've filled in it
Would have settled, harbored, promised
Slow-sweetened, laden careful keeper
Set aside for the beloved, warm bread at the hearth
Murmur through the shared cup, again, yes, please
That answers the tenderness, that fragrance sure burned slow
Sank into the deep room for more covenant whispered word
Carry it close, remain at the front door
Filled the whole house like some long breath with rising bread
We two unhurried, nourished by a kept meal
Who could get more bound off a hymn or a pulse held together?"}],"transform":{"operator":"BRIDE","verification":{"identity":"PASS","semantic_independence":"PASS","retrospective_containment":"PASS","affect_traversal":"PASS","entailment":"PASS","law_propagation":"PASS","mode":"producer_side (chain v1; verdict-derived; RETAIN-aware metering)"},"spatial_form":{}}}
